findings.message: Declare the pytest plugins required by the new test. The declared development dependencies contain neither `pytest-mock` nor `pytest-asyncio`. In an environment installed from this project's dependencies, the new test fails because the `mocker` fixture is unavailable; asynchronous execution also requires the asyncio plugin. Add both plugins to the development dependencies and lockfile.

Call the patched avatar loader through its module. Patching `chat_interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat` does not replace the function already imported into this test's namespace. This call therefore executes the real loader against `DB_PATH`, potentially creating or reading the production database and failing when avatar settings are absent. Use `chat_interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat()` to invoke the configured mock.

Exercise the real chat handler rather than the mocked dependency. This invokes the same `send_request_to_open_ai` mock whose side effect supplies every asserted result and updates history. Consequently, the test never executes `send_request_to_llm` and passes even if that handler's prompt construction, history update, or video orchestration is broken. Call the real handler, mock the LLM to return response text, and mock the voice-generation dependency as well.

This test never runs any real code. `send_request_to_llm`, the function that handles the chat interaction, is never called. Instead the test calls `chat_interface.send_request_to_open_ai`, which it replaced with a mock just above. The mock's side effect appends to CHAT_HISTORY and returns a hard-coded tuple, and the asserts then check that same tuple and list. The test passes no matter how `send_request_to_llm` behaves, so it gives no coverage of the chat flow or the history handling it claims to test. Call `await chat_interface.send_request_to_llm(...)` and mock only its external dependencies: `send_request_to_open_ai`, `send_request_to_elevenlabs`/`send_request_to_zonos` and `send_request_to_generate_video`.

The mock doesn't match the real `send_request_to_open_ai` (fetcher/fetching.py:7). The real function takes a single `messages` list and returns the LLM text response. The mock is called with 10 positional args and returns the `(msg, history, video)` tuple that `send_request_to_llm` returns. Because the mock has no spec, the signature mismatch goes unnoticed. If this mock were used against the real caller, `text_response` would be a tuple. Have it return a plain string, and use `autospec=True` so the signature is checked.

The PR says it adds two tests, one for ElevenLabs and one for Zonos, but there is only one test. Neither `send_request_to_elevenlabs` nor `send_request_to_zonos` is mocked or checked. Use `pytest.mark.parametrize` over `voice_model` ('elevenlabs', 'zonos'), call the real `send_request_to_llm`, and assert that the matching voice function was awaited with the right arguments.

`_load_avatar_infos_for_chat` is imported directly into the test module at line 2, so the later `mocker.patch("aafactory.chat.interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat", ...)` doesn't affect that local name. Line 39 therefore calls the real function, which opens the real TinyDB at DB_PATH. On a clean checkout or in CI, `avatar_page_settings_table.get(doc_id=1)` can return None, and `.get("avatar_name")` on None raises AttributeError. The test then depends on a developer's local DB, which may be why it only passes locally. Call it through the module (`chat_interface._load_avatar_infos_for_chat()`) or skip it and build the inputs directly.

The test needs the `mocker` fixture from pytest-mock and `@pytest.mark.asyncio` from pytest-asyncio, but pyproject.toml lists only pytest and pytest-cov as dev dependencies. On a fresh install, `mocker` won't be found and the async test won't run (it is skipped or fails with 'async def functions are not natively supported'). Add `pytest-mock` and `pytest-asyncio` to `[tool.poetry.group.dev.dependencies]`.

CHAT_HISTORY is cleared at the start of the test but never reset afterwards, so the global state is left behind for later tests. Use an autouse fixture, or `mocker.patch.object(chat_interface, 'CHAT_HISTORY', [])`, so each test starts and ends with an empty history. That is the isolation the PR description promises.

The description says print statements were added for debugging, but this diff has none, so the description doesn't match the change. If prints are added, prefer asserts or pytest's `-s`/logging over leaving them in the tests.
